verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this claim are the two most public datasets that exist - the price chart and a sell-side rating action - and the second one visibly moved the first. The '75% rally since mid-June' is not a hidden fact; it is quote.json, the same file I am given: mid-June closes of 8.47 (06-10) to 9.05 (06-18) rising to a 15.37 peak on 2026-08-18. Every market participant can read that. The Mizuho downgrade citing exactly that 75% figure is published wire copy, captured verbatim in docs/858fb38a...txt at 2026-08-19T10:12:08Z with the thefly.com link. And the tape then priced it: 08-18 close 15.37 -> 08-19 14.70 (-4.4% on the downgrade day) -> 09-01 14.05 -> 09-02 13.47, i.e. the stock came off 12.4% from its pre-downgrade high into the print. The base effect the hunter says nobody holds in view was repriced by 12% in the ten sessions after a broker published it. The reaction history - three of three double-digit negative prints - is not a corpus finding at all; it is the sealed baseline's own `history.moves` block, available to every reader of this run and to any market participant with a chart, and it is already expressed in the baseline's 19.11% expected move and 9.55% deadband. Most importantly, the finding's stated novelty is not a claim about the market: it is that 'a move invisible in the baseline, whose run-up fields show only -1.22% over five days and -2.34% over twenty' understates the base effect. That is a critique of the baseline's chosen lookback windows, not evidence that anyone trading the stock was unaware it had doubled. A defect in a research artefact's field set is not a market inefficiency. I hold 12 points back because the corpus genuinely carries no sell-side preview, no consensus figure and no August company disclosure, so I cannot verify whether expectations for this specific quarter had been reset after the downgrade - and that absence is a capture artefact, not a concession.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 'Mizuho downgrades Netskope on 75% rally since mid-June' - the rally, its exact magnitude and its bearish interpretation were published together on 2026-08-19, fourteen days before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The rally itself is in the bars: 8.47 on 06-10 to a 15.37 peak on 08-18, then -4.4% on the 08-19 downgrade day and a further slide to 13.47 by 09-02 (close, pre-print for an amc name), -12.4% off the high. So the base-effect concern was published and then priced over ten sessions. The three-of-three negative reaction record (-19.11%, -21.27%, -11.83%) sits in the sealed baseline and is already the source of its 19.11% expected move; the baseline is flagged `thin` (3 events) but not defective, so it is usable. The finding's own premise - that the run-up fields make the stock look flat - is a statement about the baseline's windows, not about the tape.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print source showing consensus ARR or billings estimates for this quarter had been raised after the June-August rally - i.e. that expectations, not just the price, had run ahead - rather than a broker note flagging the rally and the price then falling 12% on it.
verdicts.note_on_direction: The finding's own band 'crosses zero' and rests partly on peer read-through (CRWD/OKTA) from the same retail feed, so even its unpriced residue is unsigned.

interactions: The claim and its 'independence' note are drawn from the same StockTwits document (docs/858fb38a...txt) and point in opposite directions - the downgrade bearish, the CRWD/OKTA read-through bullish - so the cluster is one source describing a two-sided tape rather than corroboration.
corpus_limits: NTSK's capture carries no news items - it is an EDGAR filings index plus a Stocktwits dump - so there is no sell-side preview, no consensus estimate and no company guidance visible to check the expectations question against. That silence is a property of the capture's query set and I have not read it as either publication or concession. No options chain, so no implied move or skew. The only August filing is a 13G/A (2026-08-14) with no body stored.
